subject: Maths
title: Year 9 Maths Exam 8
topic: Fractions, decimals and percentages · Algebra review · Non-calculator · Higher
intro: You must not use a calculator. Show your working in the working box: method marks are given even when the final answer is wrong. Give fractions in their simplest form. "Show that" means write every step to reach the given answer. "Prove" means use algebra, not just numbers. Questions 13 to 20 go back over topics from earlier exams.

questions.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
Which fraction is equal to 0.375?
questions.ms: B1: 3/8. 0.375 = 375/1000; divide top and bottom by 125.

questions.q: Work out 0.6 × 0.03
questions.ms: Answer: 0.018. B1. 6 × 3 = 18, and there are 3 decimal places in the question, so 0.018.

questions.q: Work out 2.4 × 0.15
questions.ms: Answer: 0.36. M1 for 24 × 15 = 360 (or 2.4 × 0.1 + 2.4 × 0.05 = 0.24 + 0.12). A1 for 0.36 (3 decimal places in the question: 0.360).

questions.q:
Work out 234 + 156
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Type a mixed number with a space, like 2 3/4 (or an improper fraction like 11/4)
questions.ms: Answer: 4 7/12. M1 for 11/4 + 11/6 written with a common denominator, e.g. 33/12 + 22/12 (or 3 + 9/12 + 10/12). A1 for 4 7/12 (accept 55/12).

questions.q:
Work out 412 − 223
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Type a mixed number with a space, like 2 3/4 (or an improper fraction like 11/4)
questions.ms: Answer: 1 5/6. M1 for 27/6 − 16/6 (or 9/2 − 8/3 with common denominator 6). A1 for 1 5/6 (accept 11/6).

questions.q:
Work out 225 × 178
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Type a mixed number with a space, like 2 3/4 (or an improper fraction like 11/4)
questions.ms: Answer: 4 1/2. M1 for 12/5 × 15/8 (both changed to improper fractions). A1 for 4 1/2 (accept 9/2, 180/40 not simplified scores M1 only).

questions.q:
Work out 313 ÷ 114
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Type a mixed number with a space, like 2 3/4 (or an improper fraction like 11/4)
questions.ms: Answer: 2 2/3. M1 for 10/3 ÷ 5/4. M1 for 10/3 × 4/5 (flip the second fraction and multiply) = 40/15. A1 for 2 2/3 (accept 8/3).

questions.q: Write 0.45 as a fraction in its simplest form.
Write 238 as a decimal.
Write 740 as a percentage. (%)
questions.ms: Answer: 17.5%. B1. 7/40 = 17.5/100 (multiply top and bottom by 2.5), or 7 ÷ 40 = 0.175.

questions.q: Show that the recurring decimal 0.4̇5̇ (which means 0.454545…) is equal to 5/11.
questions.ms: M1 for x = 0.4545… and 100x = 45.4545… M1 for subtracting: 99x = 45. A1 for x = 45/99 = 5/11 (must show the simplifying step). Just dividing 5 by 11: 0 marks, because the question asks to show the decimal is 5/11.

questions.q: Write the recurring decimal 0.73̇ (which means 0.7333…) as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.ms: Answer: 11/15. M1 for 10x = 7.333… and 100x = 73.333… (two numbers with the same recurring part). M1 for 90x = 66, so x = 66/90. A1 for 11/15.

questions.q: Work out 35% of 260.
questions.ms: Answer: 91. M1 for a correct method, e.g. 10% = 26 so 30% = 78 and 5% = 13. A1 for 91.

questions.q: A jacket costs AED 240. Its price goes up by 15%. Work out the new price. (AED)

Laila buys a bike for AED 250 and later sells it for AED 320.
Work out her percentage profit. (%)
questions.ms: Answer: 28%. M1 for profit = 70. M1 for 70/250 × 100 (dividing by the ORIGINAL price). A1 for 28%. Common mistake: 70/320.

questions.q:
In a sale, all prices are reduced by 20%. A phone costs AED 1440 in the sale.
Work out the price of the phone before the sale. (AED)
questions.ms: Answer: AED 1800. M1 for 1440 = 80% (or 1440 ÷ 0.8). M1 for 1% = 18 or 10% = 180. A1 for 1800. Common mistake: adding 20% of 1440 (gives 1728), which uses the sale price instead of the original price.

questions.q:
Mona invests AED 5000 in a bank account. It pays 10% compound interest per year.
Work out how much is in the account after 3 years. (AED)
questions.ms: Answer: AED 6655. M1 for 5500 after 1 year. M1 for 6050 after 2 years (or 5000 × 1.1³ = 5000 × 1.331). A1 for 6655. Simple interest (5000 + 3 × 500 = 6500) scores 0.

questions.q:
In a class, 25 of the students walk to school and 13 come by bus. All the rest come by car.
12 students come by car. How many students are in the class?
questions.ms: Answer: 45. M1 for 2/5 + 1/3 = 11/15. M1 for car = 4/15 of the class (so 1/15 = 3 students). A1 for 45.

questions.q:
Sami says: “If a price goes up by 30% and then goes down by 30%, it goes back to the price it started at.”
Is Sami correct? Explain your answer.
questions.ms: B1: No. B1 for a reason with numbers, e.g. 100 → 130 → 130 × 0.7 = 91, or 1.3 × 0.7 = 0.91, so the price ends 9% lower. The 30% decrease is worked out on a bigger amount, so it takes off more than was added.

questions.q: x is an integer. List all the values of x such that −5 ≤ 2x − 1 < 7
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. M1 for −4 ≤ 2x < 8. M1 for −2 ≤ x < 4. A1 for the full list (−2 is included because of ≤; 4 is not, because of <).

questions.q:
Omar has AED 200. He buys 3 cinema tickets at AED 45 each. He also wants to buy some popcorn at AED 18 a box.
Write an inequality and solve it to find the greatest number of boxes of popcorn he can buy.
questions.ms: Answer: 3 boxes. M1 for 135 + 18p ≤ 200. M1 for 18p ≤ 65, so p ≤ 3.6… A1 for 3 (4 boxes would cost 135 + 72 = 207, which is too much).

questions.q: Factorise 6x2 + x − 12
questions.ms: Answer: (3x − 4)(2x + 3). M1 for splitting the middle term: 6x² + 9x − 8x − 12, or brackets that give two of the three terms. A1. Check: a × c = −72, and 9 × −8 = −72, 9 + (−8) = 1.

questions.q:
The curve y = (x − 8)(x + 2) is drawn.
Find the coordinates of the turning point of the curve.
questions.ms: Answer: (3, −25). M1 for roots x = 8 and x = −2. M1 for x = 3 (halfway between −2 and 8). A1 for y = (3 − 8)(3 + 2) = −25.

questions.q:
A rectangle has length (x + 4) cm and width (x − 1) cm. Its area is 36 cm2.
Show that x2 + 3x − 40 = 0
questions.ms: M1 for (x + 4)(x − 1) = 36. A1 for x² − x + 4x − 4 = 36, then x² + 3x − 40 = 0 (every step shown).

questions.q: Solve x2 + 3x − 40 = 0 and use your answer to find the perimeter of the rectangle. (cm)
questions.ms: Answer: 26 cm. M1 for (x + 8)(x − 5) = 0. A1 for x = 5 (reject x = −8 because the lengths would be negative). A1 for length 9 cm, width 4 cm, so perimeter 2 × (9 + 4) = 26 cm.

questions.q: Expand and simplify (x + 2)(x − 3)(x + 4)
questions.ms: Answer: x³ + 3x² − 10x − 24. M1 for expanding two brackets, e.g. (x + 2)(x − 3) = x² − x − 6. M1 for multiplying by the third bracket with at least 4 of the 6 terms correct (x³ + 4x² − x² − 4x − 6x − 24). A1 cao.

questions.q:
Solve (x − 3)(x + 2) = 4(x − 3)
Give all the solutions.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 3 or x = 2. M1 for expanding and rearranging: x² − x − 6 = 4x − 12, so x² − 5x + 6 = 0 (or taking out the common factor: (x − 3)(x + 2 − 4) = 0). M1 for (x − 3)(x − 2) = 0. A1 for both answers. Dividing both sides by (x − 3) loses the answer x = 3: max 1 mark.

questions.q: Prove that (2n + 3)2 − (2n − 3)2 is always a multiple of 12 for every integer n.
questions.ms: M1 for expanding one bracket correctly: 4n² + 12n + 9 or 4n² − 12n + 9. M1 for 24n (watch the minus sign in front of the second bracket). A1 for 24n = 12 × 2n with a statement that this is a multiple of 12. Numerical examples only: 0 marks.
